survey: A single palm tree on a sand dune, seen from slightly above eye level. Trunk: rises from the sand, leans gently to the left, then curves back right near the top; it is split into stacked ring segments whose lines bow slightly downward (fits a camera a little above them) and stay roughly at right angles to the trunk as it leans. Crown: fronds spread from one point at the top of the trunk and droop outward; mostly their upper surfaces are visible, which fits a near-eye-level view of hanging leaves. Coconuts: two hang in a cluster under the frond base, where they would attach. Ground: a low, gently rolling sand surface seen at a shallow angle; the trunk sinks into the sand with its base slightly buried; the pebbles sit flat on the sand and the palm's shadow lies flat across the dune to the right, consistent with the ground plane.
